newsitem.title: USA: Simpson plaintiffs rest case after tearful testimony.
newsitem.headline: Simpson plaintiffs rest case after tearful testimony.

text.p: Sobbing, the father of murder victim Ron Goldman glared at O.J. Simpson across a courtroom on Monday as he recalled how his son's life was cut short before he could achieve his dreams of becoming a father.
Goldman told the jurors his son wanted to marry and have children. "He decided he was going to name his first child Dakota whether it was a boy or a girl. He never had that chance," he said.
Several of the jurors appeared to be moved by the testimony, and at least two were seen dabbing their eyes during Goldman's 30 minutes on the witness stand.

Simpson was acquitted by a criminal court jury in October, 1995 of the June 12, 1994 stabbing murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Goldman. He is currently being sued for damages by the families of the victims.

Goldman's testimony concluded the plaintiffs' case after six weeks and 65 witnesses. Simpson's defence immediately began its case, calling retired detective Phillip Vannatter, who was in charge of investigating the murders, to the stand.
During Vannatter's testimony, the audiotape of Simpson's interview with police the day after the murders was played publicly for the first time.
On the tape Simpson was heard offering to give blood and explaining to Vannatter and Det. Tom Lange how blood drops came to be found at his mansion.
Vannatter was heard telling Simpson, "O.J., we've got sort of a problem. We've got some blood on and in your car, we've got some blood at your house and it's sort of a problem."
"Well, take my blood test," Simpson replied.
Asked how he got a cut on the middle finger of his left hand Simpson said he had cut it on a glass in his Chicago hotel room that morning after being told of Nicole Brown Simpson's death.
"It was cut before, but I just opened it again, I'm not sure," Simpson said. He said he recalled bleeding at home before leaving for Chicago.
"I knew I was bleeding but it was no big deal. I bleed all the time. I play golf and stuff, so there's always something, nicks and stuff, here and there," Simpson said on the tape.

Goldman, who has been outspoken in his belief that Simpson killed his 25-year-old son, occasionally turned to glare at the former athlete sitting with his attorneys about 15 feet (5 meters) away. At one point his attorney, Daniel Petrocelli, asked Goldman about a necklace with an Egyptian symbol that Ron Goldman always wore.

"It represents eternal life," he said, breaking down in sobs. "He doesn't wear it anymore. Kim (Ron's sister) wears it now." Kim Goldman, sitting in the public gallery, wept through most of her father's testmony.
Goldman was asked by Petrocelli, "Did you love your son?"
"Oh, God, yes," he replied between sobs.
Asked if he missed him, Goldman said: "More than you can imagine. There's not a day that goes by that I don't think of Ron."
Asked if his life would ever be the same again, Goldman said, "It will never, ever be the same again. There is a hole..."

The jury also saw a smiling and happy Ron Goldman in a videotape made in November, 1993, when he attended a party for his young step-sister. In the video, Ron Goldman, addressing his step-sister and other family members, said prophetically, "I'm telling you this now. God knows where I'll be in a year. I love you very much and I'll see you very soon."

The video caused Goldman to resume sobbing, as did several photographs of his son shown to the jurors on a large monitor. On two occasions it appeared that he would not be able to continue and Petrocelli asked him, "Do you think you'll be able to finish."
"I'm sorry; yes," he replied.

Goldman said his son had asked him to invest in a restaurant he wanted to start. After the murders, Goldman said he was going through his son's possessions and found plans for menus and designs for the restaurant.
"I never realised how far Ron had gone with his plans and his dreams," Goldman said.
